# Neartect

> Neartect designs a microphone's near environment — walls, floors, panels, and gratings from centimetres to metres — and computes the filter it imposes on sound arriving from a direction. Browser app, no backend; the filter comes from a Rust core compiled to WebAssembly.

## Space document

A space is JSON with `kind: "neartect.space"`. Every field has a default; unknown fields are dropped and out-of-range values are clamped.

- `air.temperatureCelsius` — sets the speed of sound.
- `microphone.position` — [east, north, up] in metres (ENU frame).
- `arrival.azimuthDegrees` (compass, toward the source), `arrival.elevationDegrees`.
- `render.sampleRateHz`, `render.lengthMilliseconds`, `render.order` (1–6).
- `surfaces[]` — `shape: "rectangle"`, `centre` [e, n, u], `widthMetres`, `heightMetres`, `yawDegrees` (direction the front faces), `tiltDegrees` (0 vertical, 90 facing up), `material`, `strength` (1 physical), `pattern` (`{ kind: "solid" }` or `{ kind: "grid", periodMetres: [across, up], barMetres: [across, up], thicknessMetres }`; a period of 0 leaves that axis without bars).

The filter is normalised to the free field: with no surfaces it is a unit impulse at time zero.
